​Here are the "worthless" elements, filler tactics, and potential red flags to watch out for:
​1. The "Proprietary Blend" (Fairy Dusting)
​The biggest issue here is the Proprietary Blend of 3,105 mg.
​The Problem: There are 16 different ingredients crammed into that single 3,105 mg number. Because manufacturers list ingredients in descending order of weight, the bulk of that weight is likely the first few ingredients (Soursop, Moringa, Neem).
​The "Worthless" Part: By the time you get down the list to high-value ingredients like Ashwagandha, Black Seed, Irish Sea Moss, and Ginger, there might only be a tiny fraction of a milligram left per serving. This is called "fairy dusting"—adding just a microscopic amount of a trendy ingredient so they can legally put it on the front of the bottle, rendering its actual health benefit essentially worthless.
​2. The Laxative "Illusion" (Senna Leaf Extract)
​Take a close look at Senna Leaf Extract in the blend.
​Senna is a potent stimulant laxative commonly used in medical treatments for severe constipation.
​Many "detox" and "gut health" supplements include it because it guarantees you will have a bowel movement, making you feel like the product is immediately "working" or "cleaning you out." In reality, using a stimulant laxative daily can make your bowel dependent on it over time.
​3. Paying Premium Prices for Kitchen Spices
​Several ingredients in this blend are basic culinary items you likely already have in your pantry:
​Garlic Bulb Powder, Bay Leaf Powder, Lemon Fruit Extract, Cinnamon Bark Powder, Ginger Root, and Black Pepper Extract.
​While these are great for you, having them ground up into a mystery-dose liquid supplement provides very little therapeutic value compared to just eating them in your diet.
​4. Added Preservatives
​Unlike the first oil which was entirely self-preserving and unrefined, the "Other Ingredients" section here lists:
​Purified Water, Citric Acid, and Potassium Sorbate.
​Potassium Sorbate is a standard chemical preservative used to prevent mold and yeast growth in water-based liquids. It's safe, but it means the product isn't the "zero-additive" formula like the black seed oil
